questions.q: What were the two main materials used to make the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro waterproof and durable?
questions.a: The two main materials were baked bricks and bitumen. A wrong answer (like "cement" or "tiles") reveals the student is applying modern construction knowledge instead of historical context.

questions.q: Why do archaeologists think the Great Bath was a significant part of the city of Mohenjo-daro?
questions.a: It was significant because it was a large, carefully engineered public structure that suggests the city had a government or authority capable of organizing large-scale construction. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks it was just a regular house tank, missing the "public" scale of the building.

questions.q: If you were exploring Mohenjo-daro, what specific features would you look for to confirm you found the Great Bath?
questions.a: Steps on two sides, a rectangular shape, surrounding rooms/verandah, and a nearby well. A student who misses these features is failing to visualize the specific archaeological description provided.

questions.q: How does the existence of a nearby well near the Great Bath explain the city's planning?
questions.a: It shows that the people did not rely on carrying water from far away, but planned the infrastructure to supply the bath directly. This reveals an understanding of "urban planning" (organized city systems).

questions.q: Could the Great Bath be used by any individual at any time? Justify your answer based on its design.
questions.a: It was likely a public building meant for group use, as indicated by its large size and the surrounding rooms. A student answering "no" without reasoning fails to connect the "public building" status with the scale of the structure.

questions.q: Imagine you are an archaeologist; if you found a similar structure in another part of the ruins, what evidence would you search for to classify it as a public building?
questions.a: Evidence would include its large size, connection to water systems (drains/wells), and its location in a central area of the city. A poor answer would focus on internal decorations rather than the utility and scale of the structure.
